title: Imported chikungunya in French travelers returning from outbreak-affected regions.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Outbreaks of chikungunya disease are unpredictable, typically episodic, and explosive. In 2025, several such outbreaks were observed and a marked increase in imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France was reported. This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks—whether officially notified or not—can cause to travelers. Methods Publicly available data from Santé Publique France were used to extract the number of chikungunya cases, and International Air Transport Association data were used for information on the number of flight tickets to estimate traveler numbers. These data were used to derive monthly rates of imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. Results Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. Peak imported rates exceeded 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers (La Réunion [April]) and 400 cases/100,000 travelers (Mayotte [May]) and remained above 100 cases/100,000 travelers for March, April, May, and June (La Réunion) and April, May, and June (Mayotte). For Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, estimated peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively, although it was noted that some outbreaks were not officially notified or were reported late. Conclusions Returning travelers to mainland France from regions facing a chikungunya outbreak in 2025 showed a substantial burden of infection and gave rise to local spread of disease, highlighting the importance of robust surveillance systems and timely outbreak notification.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rate of chikungunya infection among French travelers returning from regions with major outbreaks in 2025, including La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba. The research aimed to assess the potential burden of CHIKV outbreaks on travelers, whether officially notified or not. Using data from Santé Publique France and the International Air Transport Association, the study derived monthly importation rates of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. Results showed that the trends in imported cases closely mirrored local epidemic curves, with peak rates exceeding 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers in La Réunion and 400 cases/100,000 travelers in Mayotte. For other regions, peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively. The study concluded that returning travelers contributed significantly to the local spread of chikungunya, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance and outbreak notification systems. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of detailed limitations in the study design.

source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background Outbreaks of chikungunya disease are unpredictable, typically episodic, and explosive. In 2025, several such outbreaks were observed and a marked increase in imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France was reported. This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks—whether officially notified or not—can cause to travelers. Methods Publicly available data from Santé Publique France were used to extract the number of chikungunya cases, and International Air Transport Association data were used for information on the number of flight tickets to estimate traveler numbers. These data were used to derive monthly rates of imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. Results Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. Peak imported rates exceeded 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers (La Réunion [April]) and 400 cases/100,000 travelers (Mayotte [May]) and remained above 100 cases/100,000 travelers for March, April, May, and June (La Réunion) and April, May, and June (Mayotte). title: Content and Quality Analysis of Chikungunya Fever-Related Online Information on Social Media: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: An outbreak of chikungunya fever (CHIKF) occurred in China in 2025. The rapid increase in new cases has drawn the attention of health authorities. The outbreak also sparked widespread discussion on social media platforms. Fear-inducing and uncertain information about CHIKF circulated rapidly online, which may complicate risk communication and outbreak management efforts. In this study, we assessed the content characteristics, video quality, information reliability, transparency, and engagement of CHIKF-related short videos across the two platforms. We searched TikTok China and Bilibili using the term "chikungunya fever" and included the top 100 videos from each platform on October 9, 2025 (N = 200). Video quality was assessed using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the Video Information and Quality Index (VIQI); information reliability was evaluated using the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN); transparency was measured using the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria; and engagement was quantified using platform-based interaction metrics. Statistical analyses were performed to compare video characteristics across platforms and uploader categories, and to evaluate associations between these characteristics and quality scores. Videos from TikTok China showed higher JAMA benchmark scores, whereas videos from Bilibili achieved comparatively higher mDISCERN scores. Subgroup analyses indicated no statistical differences in engagement metrics across uploader categories, whereas quality scores differed significantly. In addition, engagement metrics showed weak correlations with video quality or reliability. The quality and reliability scores for CHIKF-related short videos on the two platforms were relatively low. The results support careful consideration of whether video quality and information reliability should be more explicitly incorporated into platform governance and content distribution strategies.

Video quality was assessed using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the Video Information and Quality Index (VIQI); information reliability was evaluated using the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN); transparency was measured using the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria; and engagement was quantified using platform-based interaction metrics. Statistical analyses were performed to compare video characteristics across platforms and uploader categories, and to evaluate associations between these characteristics and quality scores. Videos from TikTok China showed higher JAMA benchmark scores, whereas videos from Bilibili achieved comparatively higher mDISCERN scores. Subgroup analyses indicated no statistical differences in engagement metrics across uploader categories, whereas quality scores differed significantly. In addition, engagement metrics showed weak correlations with video quality or reliability. The quality and reliability scores for CHIKF-related short videos on the two platforms were relatively low. The results support careful consideration of whether video quality and information reliability should be more explicitly incorporated into platform governance and content distribution strategies.

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)基因组学中的应用,以应对在疫情期间快速、便携和准确追踪病毒多样性及传播的迫切需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于纳米孔测序在基孔肯雅病毒中的原理与应用,考察其在临床和环境样本中用于恢复完整病毒基因组和监测病毒传播的使用情况。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为病原体监测领域的重要进展,特别是在资源有限的环境中,纳米孔测序提供了一种灵活且强大的工具,用于基孔肯雅病毒的监测。

title: Overview of Chikungunya Virus Epidemiology, Biology, and Pathogenesis.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)概述、生物学及系统发育
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.
abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),一种属于Togaviridae科的虫媒α病毒,主要通过埃及伊蚊(Aedes aegypti)和白纹伊蚊(Aedes albopictus)传播。该病毒引起一种急性发热性疾病,特征为严重的、常为双侧性关节痛,可能进展为慢性肌肉骨骼疼痛,并偶有涉及心血管和神经系统系统的全身并发症。CHIKV具有球形、包膜的病毒颗粒(约70 nm),呈T = 4二十面体对称结构,包含介导受体结合和膜融合的E1/E2糖蛋白异二聚体。其正链RNA基因组(约11.8 kb)编码用于复制的非结构蛋白和用于病毒颗粒组装的结构蛋白。病毒复制发生在细胞质囊泡中,涉及基因组和亚基因组RNA的合成,随后是糖蛋白成熟和在细胞膜上出芽。从流行病学角度看,CHIKV已扩展至非洲和亚洲以外的地区,其主要传播模式由适应性进化增强其传播能力。自2013年引入美洲以来,全球发病率仍保持较高水平,2025年报告了超过180,000例确诊病例。预防策略依赖于媒介控制和疫苗接种;基于病毒样颗粒(VLP)的疫苗(如Vimkunya)显示出前景,而减毒活疫苗则面临安全性问题。目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物;现有管理措施为支持性治疗,但针对病毒复制和免疫调节的试验性疗法正在研发中。

title: Protocol for Detecting and Sequencing Chikungunya Virus from Field-Collected Mosquitoes.
abstract: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

abstract_zh: 蚊媒疾病是公共卫生领域的重要挑战,尤其是在热带地区,环境条件可能有利于蚊虫媒介的繁殖和传播。因此,对蚊虫种群中基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)进行早期和准确的检测,可以成为有效监测流行变异株和识别新病毒引入的宝贵工具。鉴于在野外捕获的蚊虫中检测蚊媒病毒的挑战,我们描述了一种集成的工作流程,用于CHIKV的分子检测和全基因组测序。该方案包括使用基于珠子的机械破碎仪对蚊虫进行匀浆,使用TRIzol试剂进行RNA提取(略有修改),使用CHIKV特异性RT-qPCR进行分子筛选,以及全基因组扩增后在Illumina平台上进行测序。尽管该方案针对单个蚊虫进行了优化,但仍能获得高质量的RNA,适用于虫媒监测和基因组分析。由于该方案能够从蚊虫样本中回收完整的CHIKV 基因组,因此可以作为基因组流行病学研究的基础,实现对病毒多样性及谱系动态的监测,并有助于早期发现新兴变异株,从而支持在流行和高风险地区及时、有针对性的公共卫生干预措施。

title: Workflow for Long-Read Amplicon Sequencing of Chikungunya Virus Using Oxford Nanopore Technology.
abstract: This protocol provides a comprehensive, step-by-step workflow for whole-genome sequencing of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using an amplicon-based strategy optimized for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platforms. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads.

title: Optimized Amplicon Strategy for Long-Read Sequencing of the Chikungunya Virus Genome.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

title: Assessing the Vector Competence for Chikungunya Virus in Mosquitoes.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito-borne virus (arbovirus), which is causing epidemic outbreaks among human populations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South- and Central America including the Caribbean. The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

title: Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test Against Chikungunya Virus Using Liver Homogenate.
abstract: We adapted the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates instead of serum. This approach enables serological investigation using tissues collected from animal carcasses as nonhuman primate ones, during arbovirus surveillance, expanding opportunities for CHIKV monitoring and strengthening epidemiological surveillance efforts.

title: Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Analysis of Ligand Binding Kinetics in Chikungunya Virus Drug Discovery.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 药物发现中基于表面等离子共振的配体结合动力学分析。
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

title: RT-RPA-Assisted CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Isothermal Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

title: Production of Viral Particles from a Chikungunya Virus Infectious Clone.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection.

title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence. This protocol highlights the use of capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) technology for the rapid detection of CHIKV. We employed Vero cells for virus propagation and utilized the MolPure Viral DNA/RNA Kit for nucleic acid extraction, successfully amplifying extracted viral RNA at 63°C for 25 min. The presence of CHIKV was indicated by a distinct yellowish-green color change, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of this protocol. Our protocol underscores the potential of LAMP technology as a rapid diagnostic tool for CHIKV, enabling timely public health interventions.

title: In Silico Drug Design of Chikungunya Antivirals: Using Consensus Methods for Virtual Screening.
abstract: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅热 抗病毒药物 的计算机药物设计:使用共识方法进行虚拟筛选。
source_body_en: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

title: Chikungunya Virus Infection in Paraffin-Embedded Tissue: Analysis of Histological Alterations and Viral Detection by Immunohistochemistry.
abstract: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 感染组织的组织学改变和病毒检测,以更好地了解其在非典型和致命病例中的 发病机制。这对于识别与 CHIKV 感染相关的损伤、炎症和细胞变性模式非常重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 CHIKV 感染个体的活检和尸检标本的组织病理学变化,重点研究病毒如何与 宿主 细胞和组织相互作用。它包括一系列标本来捕捉不同的病理表现。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及组织结构和细胞变化的组织学分析,以及检测病毒抗原的免疫组织化学。这些技术用于表征生物相关目标,例如组织样本中的免疫细胞亚群、细胞因子和分子标记。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究观察到了受感染组织中 CHIKV 诱导的损伤、炎症和细胞变性的组织学改变。免疫组织化学证实这些样本中存在病毒抗原。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了组织学和免疫组织化学方法在阐明 CHIKV 感染病理机制方面的实用性。这为病毒与 宿主 组织的相互作用提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果可以为改进的诊断方法提供信息并增强对 CHIKV 发病机制 的理解,这对于开发有针对性的 监测 和 治疗 策略至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象级别的描述,不提供详细的统计或实验数据。由于缺乏具体的数值研究结果和综合分析,证据的强度中等。

title: Assessing Chikungunya Virus Protease Activity and Pharmacological Inhibition Using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp Fluorogenic Peptide Substrate.
abstract: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.

title_zh: 使用 acc-CHIK 15 -dnp 荧光肽底物评估 基孔肯雅病毒 蛋白酶活性和药理抑制。
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.
abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 是一种蚊媒甲病毒,由于其快速传播且缺乏经批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法,对全球健康构成重大威胁。病毒非结构蛋白 2 蛋白酶 (nsP2p) 在加工病毒多蛋白以产生关键病毒酶方面发挥着关键作用,使其成为药物开发的有吸引力的目标。在本研究中,我们描述了重组 CHIKV nsP2 蛋白酶的表达和纯化,并建立了强大的荧光测定法,使用 acc-CHIK 15 -dnp 肽底物测量其酶活性。该测定能够实时监测蛋白水解裂解,并提供评估小分子抑制剂的平台。我们提出了大肠杆菌中蛋白质表达、亲和纯化和标签去除的优化条件,从而获得适合生化表征的高纯度 nsP2 蛋白酶。使用该系统,我们还提供了一个强大的方案来确定候选抑制剂的 IC50 值。这项工作为 CHIKV 蛋白酶抑制剂的高通量筛选提供了一种可重复的方法,有助于发现针对 基孔肯雅病毒 的潜在 抗病毒药物 化合物。

title: Quantification of Chikungunya Virus RNA by Real-Time RT-PCR Assay.
abstract: RT-qPCR is characterized by‌ high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, ‌enabling‌ rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. Here, we describe the use of TaqMan® probe-based one-tube Real-time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the detection and quantification of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA.

analysis.summary_en: This abstract describes the development of a TaqMan® probe‐based one‐tube real‐time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT‐qPCR) assay for detecting and quantifying Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA. The authors highlight the assay’s high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, which together enable rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. While the abstract outlines the assay’s design and the principle of fluorescence measurement proportional to PCR product, it does not provide details on study design, population, or quantitative performance data. Consequently, the report does not include results, interpretations, or implications for public‐health practice, and no limitations are discussed. The work represents a methodological advance in CHIKV diagnostics, but further data are required to assess its clinical and epidemiological utility.

title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.
abstract: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

title: Automated Counting of Chikungunya Virus-Formed Plaques.
abstract: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 形成的斑块的自动计数。
source_body_en: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática Epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes the epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas, focusing on the spread and burden of these diseases. The review included 15 studies from PubMed and SciELO between 2012 and 2025. Key findings indicate that dengue incidence has increased globally since 1990, with significant regional variations and a high burden in Latin America. Chikungunya expanded across the Americas since 2013, causing explosive urban outbreaks and persistent joint manifestations. Urbanization, the spread of Aedes species, and insecticide resistance are identified as factors that facilitate transmission. The review highlights the need for new vaccines and integrated vector control strategies to address the growing public health challenge posed by these arboviruses in tropical and subtropical cities.

title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.

abstract_zh: 疟疾和基孔肯雅热的混合感染是一种罕见的表现,对诊断提出了挑战,特别是因为两种感染都会产生全身表现和血流动力学损害。我们介绍了一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者,无既往病史,有 7 天发热、头晕、全身无力、关节痛 和呕吐病史。入院时,她出现发热、心动过速和低血压,对晶体液初始复苏的血流动力学反应不足,需要血管加压药支持。高级心血管评估显示主要是血管舒张和高动力特征,其特征是高心输出量、降低的全身血管阻力和保留的每搏输出量。左心室和右心室收缩和舒张功能仍然保留,具有足够的 TAPSE 和 MAPSE,并且没有明显的心室扩张或局部收缩力异常。心电图和心肌酶显示没有心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。研究显示严重贫血,血红蛋白水平为 6 g/dL,并且肝脾肿大。厚厚的血涂片鉴定出疟原虫。该患者的间日疟检测呈阳性,而基孔肯雅热PCR检测呈阳性,登革热检测呈阴性,证实了双重感染。开始静脉注射青蒿琥酯,随后使用蒿甲醚-本芴醇,此外还进行血管活性支持和输注两个单位的浓缩红细胞。患者的血流动力学逐渐恢复,临床病程良好。该病例强调了考虑 媒介 传播的合并感染和表征血流动力学表型以区分血管舒张性休克和心源性损害的重要性。

title: VIGILÂNCIA EPIDEMIOLÓGICA DAS ARBOVIROSES NO BRASIL: ESTRATÉGIAS ATUAIS PARA DENGUE, CHIKUNGUNYA, ZIKA E OROPOUCHE
abstract: As arboviroses representam um dos principais desafios de saúde pública no Brasil, com epidemias recorrentes de dengue, circulação sustentada de chikungunya, impacto duradouro da epidemia de zika sobre a saúde materno-infantil e, mais recentemente, a reemergência e expansão geográfica do vírus Oropouche. Em 2024, o país registrou o maior número de casos prováveis de dengue de sua história, com milhões de notificações e milhares de óbitos, em um cenário favorecido pela urbanização desordenada, pelas falhas de saneamento e pelas mudanças climáticas. A vigilância epidemiológica das arboviroses envolve a notificação compulsória, a confirmação laboratorial, a vigilância entomológica, a análise oportuna dos dados para detecção de surtos e a integração com a assistência e o controle vetorial. Nos últimos anos, novas ferramentas ampliaram as possibilidades de vigilância e controle, como a vigilância genômica, que identificou uma linhagem rearranjada do vírus Oropouche associada à sua dispersão para além da Amazônia, os sistemas de alerta precoce baseados em dados climáticos, a liberação de mosquitos infectados com Wolbachia, que reduziu a incidência de dengue em ensaio randomizado e em estudo realizado em Niterói, e a vacinação contra dengue, incluindo a vacina de dose única desenvolvida pelo Instituto Butantan. Este capítulo revisa as características epidemiológicas das principais arboviroses no Brasil, as estratégias atuais de vigilância e controle e os desafios para a integração dessas ações ao SUS.

analysis.summary_en: This chapter addresses the public health challenge posed by arboviruses in Brazil, focusing on the epidemiological characteristics of chikungunya and other related arboviruses, current surveillance and control strategies, and the integration of these efforts within the SUS. The study highlights the recurring dengue outbreaks, sustained chikungunya circulation, long-term impact of the Zika epidemic on maternal and infant health, and the recent reemergence of Oropouche virus. It outlines the methods used in arbovirus surveillance, including mandatory notification, laboratory confirmation, entomological monitoring, and data analysis for outbreak detection. The main results emphasize the expansion of surveillance tools, such as genomic surveillance, climate-based early warning systems, Wolbachia-infected mosquito releases, and the single-dose dengue vaccine developed by Butantan. The authors interpret these findings as a review of current strategies and challenges in integrating them into the SUS. The scientific and public health significance lies in the potential to reduce arbovirus incidence and improve health system responses. The evidence is general and abstract, with no specific limitations or detailed assessments provided.

title: Global Genomic Surveillance.
abstract: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.

title: Arthropod-Related Health Threats (ARHTs) and Nuisance Arthropods in North Khorasan Province, Iran: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: The arthropod vectors, such as mosquitoes, sand flies, and ticks, transmit various pathogens to humans and animals, leading to public health issues. Therefore, an effective disease surveillance system is essential to provide information on these diseases in order to monitor their trends worldwide. The current study focused on the prevalence of arthropod-borne diseases and their vectors in North Khorasan Province located in northeastern Iran, bordering Turkmenistan. A narrative literature review was conducted to analyze the status of arthropod-related health threats (ARHTs) and their vectors in this area. Sources with no time limit up to 2025 were examined from PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases using keywords like vector, arthropod, North Khorasan, and Iran. After excluding duplicates and irrelevant content, a final list of 31 papers was thoroughly evaluated. This province exhibits the occurrence of several major ARHTs, including visceral leishmaniasis, cutaneous leishmaniasis, West Nile fever, chikungunya, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Q fever, Theileria infection, equine piroplasmosis, dirofilariasis, Dipylidium caninum infection, fascioliasis, hymenolepiasis, scorpionism, spider bites, pediculosis, and myiasis. Given the complex and diverse ecosystem of North Khorasan, implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, thus enabling timely and efficient management of these health threats.

analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes the complexity and diversity of the ecosystem in North Khorasan, which may affect disease transmission dynamics. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, including chikungunya virus, to enable timely and efficient management of these health threats.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the prevalence of arthropod-borne diseases, including chikungunya virus, in North Khorasan Province, Iran. It highlights the role of vectors such as mosquitoes, sand flies, and ticks in disease transmission and emphasizes the need for robust surveillance systems. The study identifies chikungunya fever and infection as significant health threats in the region, alongside other diseases. While the review provides a general overview of the area's health challenges, it lacks detailed comparative data on surveillance strategies and transmission mechanisms. The findings suggest that tailored and innovative approaches are necessary to address these threats effectively.

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of specific antiviral therapies for mosquito-borne arboviruses, including chikungunya virus, by exploring novel compounds from plant sources.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a bioactivity-guided approach to screen methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species for antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells, with a focus on chikungunya virus.
analysis.methods: The researchers used bioactivity-guided screening, fractionation, and purification techniques to isolate compounds, followed by structural characterization using UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy, and functional assays to assess antiviral activity.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Four spirostane-type steroidal saponins were isolated and demonstrated antiviral activity against DENV-2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that spirostane saponins could serve as promising antiviral scaffolds, offering potential for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents against multiple arboviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into plant-derived compounds as therapeutic options for chikungunya virus and other related arboviruses, potentially contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro findings and does not address in vivo efficacy or clinical translation, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins as antiviral agents against chikungunya virus and other arboviruses. The research highlights the growing global health burden of mosquito-borne viruses, including chikungunya, and the lack of specific therapies. A bioactivity-guided approach was used to screen extracts from eight Solanaceae species, identifying compounds that inhibit DENV-2 replication in Vero cells. Structural characterization and functional assays confirmed the antiviral activity of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, with evidence suggesting their efficacy against multiple arboviruses. The findings indicate that these compounds could be promising scaffolds for developing broad-spectrum antiviral agents. However, the study is limited to in vitro results, which restricts the strength of the evidence to moderate. The results may inform future research into plant-derived therapies for chikungunya and related viruses, contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用生物活性引导的方法来筛选来自八种茄科物种的甲醇提取物,以检测 Vero 细胞中针对 DENV-2 的 抗病毒药物 活性,重点是 基孔肯雅病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用生物活性引导的筛选、分馏和纯化技术来分离化合物,然后使用 UPLC-DAD-MS 和 1D/2D NMR 光谱进行结构表征,并进行功能测定以评估 抗病毒药物 活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 五种提取物显着降低了病毒感染性,其中包括 Solanum ovalifolium 和 Cestrum sp。在非细胞毒性浓度下实现完全抑制。分离出四种螺罗坦型甾体皂苷,并证明了 抗病毒药物 对抗 DENV-2 的活性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,螺罗坦皂苷可以作为有前途的 抗病毒药物 支架,为开发针对多种虫媒病毒的广谱 抗病毒药物 药物提供了潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该结果为进一步研究植物源化合物作为 基孔肯雅病毒 和其他相关虫媒病毒的治疗选择奠定了基础,可能有助于 监测 和 治疗 策略。

source_body_en: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
abstract_zh: 由蚊子传播的虫媒病毒,包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特定抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用生物活性引导的方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行筛选,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中的DENV-2。五种提取物显著降低了病毒感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过UPLC-DAD-MS和1D/2D NMR光谱法进行了表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制了DENV的复制,表现为病毒RNA水平的显著降低、NS1和NS3蛋白表达的减少以及传染性病毒滴度的下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白加工一致。分子对接分析支持了这些发现,预测了这些化合物与关键病毒酶的有利相互作用,特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其对多种虫媒病毒具有交叉疗效。综上所述,这些发现将螺甾烷皂苷识别为有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过探索植物来源的新化合物,解决针对蚊媒虫媒病毒(包括基孔肯雅病毒)缺乏特异性抗病毒药物的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用生物活性引导的方法来筛选来自八种茄科物种的甲醇提取物,以检测 Vero 细胞中针对 DENV-2 的 抗病毒药物 活性,重点是 基孔肯雅病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用生物活性引导的筛选、分馏和纯化技术来分离化合物,然后使用 UPLC-DAD-MS 和 1D/2D NMR 光谱进行结构表征,并进行功能测定以评估 抗病毒药物 活性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 五种提取物显着降低了病毒感染性,其中包括 Solanum ovalifolium 和 Cestrum sp。在非细胞毒性浓度下实现完全抑制。分离出四种螺罗坦型甾体皂苷,并证明了 抗病毒药物 对抗 DENV-2 的活性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,螺罗坦皂苷可以作为有前途的 抗病毒药物 支架,为开发针对多种虫媒病毒的广谱 抗病毒药物 药物提供了潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该结果为进一步研究植物源化合物作为 基孔肯雅病毒 和其他相关虫媒病毒的治疗选择奠定了基础,可能有助于 监测 和 治疗 策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外研究结果,不涉及体内疗效或临床转化,这将证据的强度降至中等。

title: Integrating developmental traits, morphometrics and machine learning for sex classification of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae).
abstract: Abstract Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762), the primary vector for dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever, requires precise sex separation for the effective application of the sterile insect technique. This study integrates developmental biology, morphometric analysis and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Ae. aegypti pupae and adults. We evaluated developmental parameters across six generations of the Old Balara strain. Morphometric data from pupae and adults, including pupal cephalothorax dimensions, pupal length, pupal weight, adult wing length and adult thorax length, were collected to assess their correlations. Pupal morphometrics (cephalothorax dimensions and pupal length and weight) were used to train nine ML models for pupal sex classification. Males pupated significantly earlier (5.61 ± 0.10 days) than females (6.40 ± 0.16 days). In the absence of mating, females lived longer (22.63 ± 0.42 days) than males (20.13 ± 0.34 days). After mating, longevity declined, with females showing a 10.34% reduction (2.34 days) and males a 32.94% reduction (6.63 days). Across all morphometric parameters (cephalothorax length, width and perimeter in mm; cephalothorax area in mm 2 ; pupal length in mm; pupal weight in mg; adult wing length in mm; thorax length in mm), females were significantly larger than males. Pupal cephalothorax perimeter and area strongly correlated with adult thorax and wing lengths ( R 2 up to 0.88), indicating their predictive value for adult size. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines and Naïve Bayes achieved 100% accuracy in pupal sex classification on the test set. Integrating morphometric analysis with machine learning significantly enhances sex sorting precision for the sterile insect technique, improving mosquito control efficiency by ensuring only males are released. Future research should explore incorporating image‐based data and advanced machine learning techniques to further refine these methods across diverse mosquito populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop precise sex separation methods for Aedes aegypti to enhance the sterile insect technique, which is crucial for controlling the vector of dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study integrated developmental biology, morphometric analysis, and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Aedes aegypti pupae and adults across six generations of the Old Balara strain.
analysis.methods: Developmental parameters and morphometric data were collected and used to train nine machine learning models for pupal sex classification. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, and Naïve Bayes achieved 100% accuracy in classification.
analysis.main_results: Males pupated earlier than females, and females lived longer than males in the absence of mating. After mating, longevity declined for both sexes. Morphometric parameters strongly correlated with adult size, indicating their predictive value.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that integrating morphometric analysis with machine learning significantly enhances sex sorting precision for the sterile insect technique, improving mosquito control efficiency.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective sex sorting methods for the sterile insect technique, which is crucial for controlling the spread of dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a single strain and the absence of a detailed discussion on generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study integrated developmental biology, morphometric analysis, and machine learning to develop precise sex separation methods for Aedes aegypti, enhancing the sterile insect technique for vector control of dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发埃及伊蚊的精确性别分离方法,以增强昆虫不育技术,这对于控制登革热、寨卡、基孔肯雅热和黄热病的 媒介 至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究整合了发育生物学、形态测量分析和机器学习,以区分六代老巴拉拉菌株中埃及伊蚊蛹和成虫的性别。
elements_zh.methods: 收集发育参数和形态测量数据并用于训练九个用于蛹性别分类的机器学习模型。逻辑回归,支持媒介机器,朴素贝叶斯实现了100%的分类准确率。
elements_zh.main_results: 雄性比雌性化蛹早,在没有交配的情况下,雌性比雄性寿命更长。交配后,两性的寿命都会下降。形态测量参数与成人体型密切相关,表明它们的预测价值。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究表明,形态测量分析与机器学习相结合可显着提高昆虫不育技术的性别分选精度,提高蚊虫控制效率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为昆虫不育技术开发更有效的性别分选方法提供信息,这对于控制登革热、寨卡病毒、基孔肯雅热和黄热病的传播至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括使用单一菌株以及缺乏对普遍性的详细讨论。由于研究范围有限,证据强度中等。

title_zh: 整合发育性状、形态测量学和机器学习来对埃及伊蚊(双翅目:蚊科)进行性别分类。
source_body_en: Abstract Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762), the primary vector for dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever, requires precise sex separation for the effective application of the sterile insect technique. This study integrates developmental biology, morphometric analysis and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Ae. aegypti pupae and adults. We evaluated developmental parameters across six generations of the Old Balara strain. Morphometric data from pupae and adults, including pupal cephalothorax dimensions, pupal length, pupal weight, adult wing length and adult thorax length, were collected to assess their correlations. Pupal morphometrics (cephalothorax dimensions and pupal length and weight) were used to train nine ML models for pupal sex classification. Males pupated significantly earlier (5.61 ± 0.10 days) than females (6.40 ± 0.16 days). In the absence of mating, females lived longer (22.63 ± 0.42 days) than males (20.13 ± 0.34 days). After mating, longevity declined, with females showing a 10.34% reduction (2.34 days) and males a 32.94% reduction (6.63 days). Across all morphometric parameters (cephalothorax length, width and perimeter in mm; cephalothorax area in mm 2 ; pupal length in mm; pupal weight in mg; adult wing length in mm; thorax length in mm), females were significantly larger than males. Pupal cephalothorax perimeter and area strongly correlated with adult thorax and wing lengths ( R 2 up to 0.88), indicating their predictive value for adult size. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines and Naïve Bayes achieved 100% accuracy in pupal sex classification on the test set. Integrating morphometric analysis with machine learning significantly enhances sex sorting precision for the sterile insect technique, improving mosquito control efficiency by ensuring only males are released. Future research should explore incorporating image‐based data and advanced machine learning techniques to further refine these methods across diverse mosquito populations.

title: Molecular Cloning and Reverse Genetics.
abstract: This chapter describes a detailed molecular biology protocol for introducing specific point mutations into the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome using a reverse genetics strategy. The method utilizes an overlapping PCR-based approach to generate a mutated DNA fragment, which is then cloned into a pre-engineered CHIKV infectious clone plasmid. The protocol covers all major steps, from the initial PCRs to create the mutated insert to its digestion and ligation into the vector. It also includes procedures for bacterial transformation, colony screening via PCR and Sanger sequencing to confirm the mutation, and plasmid purification via miniprep. The document is structured with a clear introduction, a list of all required reagents and equipment, and a step-by-step methods section.

title: Bionomics aspects of major arbovirus vectors, Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus in different ecoclimatic environments of Cameroon
abstract: Abstract Background Aedes mosquitoes transmit dengue, Zika and chikungunya viruses, which remain major public health concerns globally and in Africa. Effective prevention and control rely on a sound understanding of vector bio-ecology. In Cameroon, little is known about the bio-ecology and behaviour of Aedes vectors. This study aimed to update the geographical distribution, resting behaviour, host-seeking behaviour and natural infections by arboviruses in Aedes spp. vectors in Cameroon. Methods Sampling was carried out in eight locations across the country. Immature stages of Aedes were collected in seven localities, transported to the insectary, reared to adult, identified, counted, and grouped by species to determine their distribution. Resting behaviour was assessed through inside houses and outdoor aspirations using Prokopack and CDC backpack aspirators. Host-seeking activity was evaluated with BG-Sentinel traps. Natural infections with dengue, chikungunya and Zika viruses were determined by real-time quantitative Multiplex PCR and RT-PCR. Chi-squared test was used to compare abundances Results 17,040 adults identified from the immature stages of Aedes spp. albopictus , 48.93% Ae. aegypti , and 0.02% Ae. We noted the first identification of Aedes albopictus in Meiganga since its introduction in Cameroon. Aedes aegypti was present in all the localities surveyed, while Ae. albopictus had a distribution limited to the southern part of the country below latitude 6.4°N. Resting and biting behaviours have shown that both species are essentially exophilic and exophagous. Aedes aegypti preferred to rest in used tyres, while Ae. albopictus had a wide range of preferred resting sites (natural vegetation, used tyres, banana plants, mixed resting places). Both species of mosquito bite throughout the day between 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., with essentially unimodal host-seeking activity, with a major peak of activity in the afternoon between 1 p.m. Natural infections by dengue, chikungunya and Zika viruses showed one positive pool of Ae. aegypti for serotype 3 of dengue virus (DENV-3). Conclusion These results provide an important knowledge base on the bionomics of Aedes mosquitoes in different localities in Cameroon and also establish evidence base essential for designing and implementing targeted arboviral diseases surveillance and vector control strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在更新伊蚊属虫媒病毒的地理分布、静息行为、宿主 寻找行为和自然感染。在喀麦隆,解决该国对这些 媒介 缺乏了解的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在喀麦隆全国八个地点对伊蚊属的未成熟阶段进行采样。收集并饲养成虫以进行识别和分布分析。使用各种方法评估休息和寻找 宿主 的行为,并确定登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒的自然感染。
elements_zh.methods: 在七个地点收集了未成熟阶段的昆虫,运输到昆虫饲养场,饲养成成虫并进行鉴定。使用 Prokopack 和 CDC 背包吸气器通过室内和室外呼吸来评估休息行为。使用 BG-Sentinel 陷阱评估 宿主 寻找活动。通过实时定量多重 PCR 和 RT-PCR 确定虫媒病毒的自然感染。
elements_zh.main_results: 鉴定出未成熟期伊蚊成虫17,040只,其中伊蚊占48.93%。埃及伊蚊和 0.02% Ae。所有调查地点均存在埃及伊蚊,而伊蚊则存在于所有调查地点。白纹伊蚊在该国南部地区发现。两个物种均表现出嗜外食性和外食性行为,其中 Ae.埃及伊蚊更喜欢二手轮胎和埃及伊蚊。白纹伊蚊有广泛的首选栖息地。单个 Ae 阳性池。已鉴定出携带 DENV-3 的埃及伊蚊。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了有关喀麦隆不同地区伊蚊生物学特性的重要知识,为设计和实施有针对性的虫媒病毒性疾病 监测 和 媒介 控制策略奠定了证据基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为喀麦隆虫媒病毒疾病 监测、诊断 和 媒介 控制策略提供信息,通过增强对 媒介 生物生态学的了解,为公共卫生做出贡献。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因使用非随机抽样方法且缺乏详细的统计分析而受到限制。由于该研究的观察性质,证据强度中等。

title: Emerging or Newly Detected? Rethinking Infectious Disease Outbreaks in North Africa
abstract: North Africa sits where climate change, armed conflict and cross-border mobility meet, and each of these moves pathogens. Yet outbreaks in the region are often recognized late, through travel surveillance abroad, single-hospital studies or reference laboratories rather than routine national reporting. This editorial, which opens the special issue on emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks in North Africa, reviews three microbial fronts: arboviruses such as West Nile, dengue and chikungunya viruses; antimicrobial resistance and conflict-driven cholera; and fungal pathogens, including Candida auris. It summarizes eleven outbreaks reported in the region since 2012 and how each came to light. The gap between reported and actual burden can be large: in eastern Sudan in 2018, surveillance counted 13,978 chikungunya cases, whereas the epidemic was later estimated to have affected about 487,600 people. The editorial argues that many infections called emerging in North Africa are newly detected rather than new, and that the main gap lies in laboratory and surveillance capacity. It calls for integrated One Health surveillance and wider access to molecular and fungal diagnostics.
journal: Sebha University Journal of Medical Sciences

abstract_zh: 北非位于气候变化、武装冲突和跨境流动交汇的地方,每一种因素都会传播病原体。然而,该地区的 暴发 通常通过出国旅行、单家医院研究或参考实验室而不是常规的国家报告而较晚得到认可。这篇社论开启了关于北非新出现和重新出现的传染病 暴发 的特刊,回顾了三个微生物前沿:西尼罗河、登革热和 基孔肯雅病毒 等虫媒病毒;抗菌素耐药性和冲突引发的霍乱;和真菌病原体,包括耳念珠菌。它总结了自 2012 年以来该地区报告的 11 起 暴发 事件以及每起事件的曝光过程。报告的负担与实际负担之间的差距可能很大:2018 年,监测 统计在苏丹东部有 13,978 例基孔肯雅热病例,而后来估计该流行病影响了约 487,600 人。社论认为,许多被称为北非新出现的感染是新发现的而不是新的,主要差距在于实验室和 监测 的能力。它呼吁整合 One Health 监测 以及更广泛地获得分子和真菌诊断。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 这篇社论探讨了北非传染病的出现和重新出现,重点关注 基孔肯雅病毒 及其相关谱系。它探讨了如何识别 暴发 以及准确评估其真实负担的挑战。

title: Screening of Antiviral Agents Against CHIKV Using Reporter Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.
abstract: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

abstract_zh: 亲和纯化质谱 (AP-MS) 是一种强大的蛋白质组学方法,用于剖析病毒和 宿主 之间的相互作用网络。传统的 AP-MS 采用病毒蛋白的过度表达作为诱饵来丰富 宿主 相互作用子。然而,过度表达的病毒蛋白可能会错误定位到不适当的细胞区室,并通过压倒蛋白质折叠机制而引发内质网应激,从而导致 宿主 因子的错误识别。为了克服这些限制,我们引入了一种基于直接感染表位标记的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV/myc-E2) 的 AP-MS 策略,我们用它成功地发现了 CHIKV 细胞 储存宿主 巨噬细胞中的两个新的 抗病毒药物 因子。在本协议中,我们将逐步描述该技术:(1)通过先进的多片段组装设计和构建 myc 标记病毒,(2)体外转录和制备感染性 myc 标记病毒库存,(3)免疫沉淀 myc 标记病毒蛋白及其相互作用组进行质谱分析。该策略能够在生理相关背景下准确识别病毒相互作用因子,为未来使用标记病毒的蛋白质组学研究提供框架。

title: A Restriction-Free Cloning Approach for Molecular Engineering of Plasmids.
abstract: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.

title_zh: 质粒分子工程的无限制克隆方法。
source_body_en: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.
abstract_zh: 使用高持续性、高保真度 DNA 聚合酶通过 PCR 扩增进行分子克隆代表了一种用于精确操作核酸序列的稳健且通用的技术。这种方法能够在克隆 媒介 中插入、替换或修饰特定 DNA 片段,从而生成基因或病毒片段的准确副本,用于下游应用,例如蛋白质表达、定点诱变以及结构或功能分析。使用持续的高保真聚合酶可显着减少碱基替换错误的发生,确保整个扩增过程中的序列完整性。传统上,限制性内切酶被用来促进定向克隆。然而,替代方法允许诱变,而不需要独特和特定的限制位点,并且可以应用于几乎任何克隆或无缝 DNA 组装策略。在本章中,我们描述了一种基于无限制性内切酶和无连接 PCR 的方案,广泛适用于任何环状 媒介。该方法能够对 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 基因组 进行定向诱变,为生成适合病毒学和分子研究的突变体构建体提供快速、高效和可靠的策略。

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

abstract_zh: 虫媒病毒仍然是世界许多地区公共卫生的重大挑战。尽管具有共同的流行病学特征,但每种虫媒病毒性疾病都表现出不同的细胞向性和激活模式,并发展为尚未完全阐明的免疫病理学结果。要更深入地了解这些过程,需要能够表征通常复杂的细胞反应的方法。在这种背景下,流式细胞术成为一种有价值的工具,可以表征异质细胞群、评估活化和增殖标记、量化炎症介质以及检测细胞死亡途径。通过整合这些参数,流式细胞术可以增强我们对虫媒病毒发病机制的了解,阐明其细胞向性,并了解免疫应答的感染情况。这篇方法论文章概述了将该技术应用于受基孔肯雅热、登革热、黄热病和寨卡病毒感染的不同目标组织的主要步骤,强调了最有效的策略。
